en.title: Good News Network Highlights Historical Milestones on October 31
en.dek: Good News Network lists milestones from Zaha Hadid's birth to Leiden University Libraries opening and Mount Rushmore's completion.
facts: Zaha Hadid was born on October 31, 1950.
Zaha Hadid founded Zaha Hadid Architects in 1980.
Mount Rushmore carving was completed in 1941.
body: Zaha Hadid was born on October 31, 1950, in Baghdad. Good News Network described her as the "Queen of Curves" and said she liberated architectural geometry. She was knighted by Queen Elizabeth II for her contributions to world architecture.

In 1980 she founded Zaha Hadid Architects in London. Between 2000 and 2010 she completed the Bridge Pavilion in Zaragoza, the Heydar Aliyev Center in Baku, the Guangzhou Opera House, and the Vienna University of Economics and Business Library. These works earned her major prizes. The firm continues to build notable structures worldwide.

Leiden University Libraries opened in 1587, 439 years before the Good News Network article. According to scholar Nicholas A. Basbanes, the library is an essential benchmark for modern scholarly libraries. It pioneered the first printed catalogue, the first special collections, and the first universal library. Its humanistic approach to education has been highlighted by Basbanes.

Mount Rushmore's carving of four presidents was completed in 1941, 85 years before the article. The sculpture brings in millions of visitors to the Black Hills of Keystone, South Dakota. The heads of George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt, and Abraham Lincoln stand 60 feet high.
en.context: Good News Network publishes daily highlights of positive historical events. The October 31 edition lists milestones from architecture to libraries to national monuments.

problemsFixed: Repeated sentence openings and four short declarative sentences in a row.
Unnecessary filler and lack of varied sentence length.
Inconsistent use of dates and lack of exact dates for some events.
